def-hh-right-right-hopf-module-and-coinv:
## Definition

Let $k$ be a field, $H$ a Hopf algebra over $k$, and $M$ a $k$-vector space. A **right $H$-module structure** on $M$ is a bilinear map $(m,h)\mapsto mh$ satisfying $(mh)g=m(hg)$ and $m1_H=m$. A **right $H$-comodule structure** is a linear map $\rho:M\to M\otimes H$ satisfying
$$
(\rho\otimes\operatorname{id}_H)\rho=(\operatorname{id}_M\otimes\Delta)\rho,\qquad (\operatorname{id}_M\otimes\varepsilon)\rho=\operatorname{id}_M.
$$
Write $\rho(m)=\sum m_0\otimes m_1$ and $\Delta(h)=\sum h_1\otimes h_2$, where each expression denotes a finite tensor sum. The pair of structures makes $M$ a **right-right Hopf module** if it satisfies
$$
\rho(mh)=\sum m_0h_1\otimes m_1h_2\qquad(m\in M,\ h\in H).
$$
A **morphism of right-right Hopf modules** is a linear map preserving both the right action and right coaction. The **coinvariants** are the subset
$$
M^{\operatorname{co}H}:=\{m\in M:\rho(m)=m\otimes1_H\}.
$$
The next lemma proves that this subset is a $k$-subspace. No finite-dimensionality of $H$ or $M$, and no bijectivity of the antipode, is part of the definition.
lem-hh-coinvariants-form-a-subspace:
## Statement

For a right-right Hopf module $M$ over a Hopf algebra $H$ over a field $k$, the subset $M^{\operatorname{co}H}=\{m\in M:\rho(m)=m\otimes1_H\}$ is a $k$-linear subspace of $M$.
lem-hh-free-right-right-hopf-module:
## Statement

Let $k$ be a field, $H$ a Hopf algebra over $k$, and $V$ any $k$-vector space. On $V\otimes H$ define
$$
(v\otimes h)g:=v\otimes hg,\qquad \rho(v\otimes h):=\sum(v\otimes h_1)\otimes h_2.
$$
These maps make $V\otimes H$ a right-right Hopf module. No finite-dimensionality or choice of basis for $V$ is needed.
lem-hh-hopf-module-coinvariant-projectio:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a right-right Hopf module over a Hopf algebra $H$ over a field $k$. Define
$$
P:M\to M,\qquad P(m):=\sum m_0S(m_1).
$$
Then $P$ is a linear map with image in $M^{\operatorname{co}H}$, it fixes every coinvariant, and hence $P^2=P$. No bijectivity of $S$ is assumed.
thm-hh-fundamental-theorem-of-hopf-modul:
## Statement

Let $H$ be a Hopf algebra over a field $k$ and $M$ a right-right Hopf module over $H$. Equip $M^{\operatorname{co}H}\otimes H$ with the free right-right Hopf-module structure. The map
$$
\alpha:M^{\operatorname{co}H}\otimes H\to M,\qquad n\otimes h\mapsto nh,
$$
is an isomorphism of right-right Hopf modules, with inverse
$$
\beta:M\to M^{\operatorname{co}H}\otimes H,\qquad \beta(m)=\sum P(m_0)\otimes m_1,
$$
where $P(m)=\sum m_0S(m_1)$. No bijectivity assumption on $S$ is used.
lem-hh-coinvariants-of-free-hopf-module:
## Statement

Let $V$ be any $k$-vector space and $H$ a Hopf algebra over $k$. For the free Hopf module $V\otimes H$ with coaction on the $H$ factor,
$$
(V\otimes H)^{\operatorname{co}H}=\{v\otimes1_H:v\in V\}.
$$
The map $i:V\to(V\otimes H)^{\operatorname{co}H}$, $i(v)=v\otimes1_H$, is an isomorphism with inverse the restriction of $q:=\operatorname{id}_V\otimes\varepsilon$.
cor-hh-hopf-module-functor-equivalence:
## Statement

Let $H$ be a Hopf algebra over a field $k$. The coinvariants functor from right-right Hopf modules over $H$ to $k$-vector spaces and the free Hopf-module functor $V\mapsto V\otimes H$ are inverse equivalences. Their natural unit is $\eta_V(v)=v\otimes1_H$, and their natural counit is $\epsilon_M(n\otimes h)=nh$.
